election_dates.primarySnippet: Tex. Elec. Code § 41.007(a): The general primary election date is the first Tuesday in March in each even-numbered year.
election_dates.generalSnippet: Tex. Elec. Code § 41.002: The general election for state and county officers shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in even-numbered years.

state_background_check.value: No — Texas's felony-disqualification requirement (Tex. Elec. Code § 141.001(a)(4)) applies only to "a public elective office in this state" by its own text, not federal office; separately, the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates either way
state_background_check.snippet: Tex. Elec. Code § 141.001: "(a) To be eligible to be a candidate for, or elected or appointed to, a public elective office in this state, a person must: ... (4) have not been finally convicted of a felony from which the person has not been pardoned or otherwise released from the resulting disabilities..." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

platform.value: Repeal the federal income tax, abolish the IRS, and replace them with nothing.
platform.snippet: I will work to repeal the income tax, abolish the IRS, and replace them with nothing.

platform.value: Support an Ellis Island-style immigration system with free movement of people across international borders, where foreigners are welcome after being checked for a criminal record and communicable diseases, and abolish ICE.
platform.snippet: the solution is to embrace economic liberty and free markets. That means the free movement of people across international borders, with an Ellis-Island-style immigration system where foreigners are welcome to come here but must be checked for a criminal record and communicable diseases before being let in.

platform.value: Abolish ICE and limit CBP to the border and points of entry, not operating inland.
platform.snippet: I believe that ICE should be abolished, the sooner the better. CBP should be limited to the border and other points of entry (like airports and seaports) and not operate inland as far as 100 miles as currently authorized.

platform.value: Bring all troops home and end America's role as the world's policeman.

platform.value: Oppose government-mandated age limits on social media and age verification laws that force providers to identify every user.
platform.snippet: I oppose government-mandated age limits on social media or other internet use. I oppose age verification laws that supposedly protect children from "harmful" material, but that in fact force providers to identify every user, thus violating everyone's privacy.

platform.value: Oppose digital identification requirements that integrate personal ID, medical records, banking records, biometric data, or other unique identifiers, and oppose any government social credit systems.
platform.snippet: I oppose digital identification requirements that integrate personal ID, medical records, banking records, biometric data, or other unique identifiers, either mandated by or for use by government. I oppose any government "social credit" systems that use technology to assess the reputation of individuals based on their behaviors, financial records, and legal compliance.

platform.value: Oppose the requirement that automakers install a kill switch on all new vehicles starting in 2027.
platform.snippet: I am opposed to the new requirement that automakers install a "kill switch" on all new vehicles starting in 2027.

platform.value: Running to repeal as many laws as possible, not to be a lawmaker.
platform.snippet: There are too many laws. I am not running for U.S. Senator to be a "lawmaker." I am running to repeal as many laws as I can.

bio_summary.value: I am not running for U.S. Senator to be a "lawmaker." I am running to repeal as many laws as I can. See more There are basic laws that we all know to follow. Crimes such as murder, rape, robbery and fraud should be illegal. But there are actually thousands of pages of laws, which turn non-violent personal behavior into crimes, or which create countless bureaucratic administrative offenses.

platform.value: Will take on Big Pharma and Big Food, increase transparency in food and healthcare systems, and put well-being of Americans ahead of corporate profits

platform.value: Will fight to cut taxes and stop wasteful spending

platform.value: Will help bring down costs and remove harmful regulations designed to hurt energy companies
platform.snippet: After four years of Joe Biden causing skyrocketing inflation and declaring war on American energy, Ken Paxton will help bring down costs and remove harmful regulations designed to hurt our energy companies.

platform.value: Will support crypto innovation with a clear, pro-growth regulatory framework and passing the CLARITY Act
platform.snippet: America must be the crypto capital of the world and support innovation and growth. Digital assets are one of the defining frontiers changing the world, and the United States cannot afford to fall behind. Achieving that requires a clear, pro-growth regulatory framework, and passing critical legislation like the CLARITY Act is key to giving innovators certainty to build and scale.

bio_summary.value: Ken Paxton is a fearless conservative, a battle-tested Attorney General, and a relentless defender of Texas values. He's taken on Biden's overreach, fought for election integrity, and never bent a knee — even as the establishment came after him time and time again. Now, he's bringing that same Texas toughness to the U.S. Senate.

platform.value: Cites growing up in East Austin raised by a single mother who worked overtime at a hotel, and his own experience as a public school teacher struggling with student and medical debt, as the reason he believes government should serve working people instead of giant corporations
platform.snippet:
I was born to a single mom who worked overtime at a hotel to support me. We lived in a little apartment in East Austin. There wasn’t room for a nursery, so I slept in a crib in her closet. She was so proud of that closet. She decorated it with pictures and toys — no one was gonna tell her it wasn’t a nursery!

As a former public school teacher, I know what it’s like to work early mornings and late nights in an underpaid, stressful job. I know what it’s like to be crushed by student debt and medical debt. And I know what it’s like to feel like the system isn’t working for you.
We need a government that serves working people instead of giant corporations.

platform.value: Says that as a legislator he has fought for working Texans, stood up to billionaire mega-donors and special interests, and passed major legislation lowering the cost of prescription drugs, housing, and childcare
platform.snippet: As a legislator, I have fought for working Texans, I’ve stood up to billionaire mega-donors and special interests, and I’ve worked to cut bureaucratic red tape — passing major legislation to lower the cost of prescription drugs, housing, and childcare. Now I’m ready to take this fight to the U.S. Senate.

platform.value: Wants a fairer tax system that makes giant corporations and the wealthiest Americans pay their fair share -- including higher taxes on billionaires' income and capital gains, ending 'buy, borrow, die' wealth-growth loopholes, raising the corporate tax rate, ending carried-interest loopholes, and taxing corporate stock buybacks -- so taxes can be cut for working families and small businesses
platform.snippet: Create a fairer tax system: Make giant corporations and the wealthiest Americans pay their fair share of taxes. (That way, we can cut taxes for working families and small businesses.) Make billionaires pay their fair share in taxes — including by imposing a higher tax on their income and capital gains and ending the dubious “buy, borrow, die” loopholes that billionaires use to grow untaxed wealth. Make corporations pay their fair share in taxes — including by raising the corporate tax rate (it has fallen by HALF since the mid-1980s!), ending the “carried interest” tax loopholes that allow hedge funds to avoid paying billions that they owe, and rolling back other extreme tax breaks that allow the largest corporations to pay $0 in federal income taxes. Raise the tax on corporate stock buybacks, which corporations use to artificially inflate their stock prices instead of making investments in research and development or to pay their employees the full value of their work.

platform.snippet: Increase wages for workers, not CEOs: Raise the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour, and incentivize CEOs to pay fair wages by creating a special tax on corporations that pay their top executives more than 250 times their median worker’s salary.

platform.value: Taught 6th-grade language arts on the Westside of San Antonio, one of Texas's poorest zip codes, before running for office, and says he had 45 kids in one classroom (some sitting on the air conditioning unit) after the Legislature cut $5 billion from public education
platform.snippet:
Before I ran for office, I was a public school teacher. I taught 6th-grade language arts on the Westside of San Antonio — one of Texas’s poorest zip codes.

When I entered the classroom, the Texas Legislature had just gutted the public education budget by $5 billion — so I had 45 kids in one classroom. There weren’t enough desks for everyone, so some of my students sat on the air conditioning unit.

In each of my four terms in the Texas House of Representatives, I served on the Public Education Committee — partnering with parents, teachers, and students to increase teacher pay, improve early childhood education, expand career and technical education, and more.

platform.value: Was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at 28 after collapsing during a 25-mile campaign walk across his House district, and says his first 30-day insulin supply cost $684 -- despite it costing companies only about $10 per vial to produce -- which he had to put on a credit card
platform.snippet:
When I was 28 years old, I almost died.

I was running in my first race for the Texas House. I decided to walk the entire length of my district — 25 miles in one day — holding town halls along the way. I wasn’t worried about my ability to finish the walk — I hike Big Bend every year!

But about halfway through, I started feeling nauseous and fatigued. I threw up a couple of times on the way, but figured I was just dehydrated. Somehow, I finished.

When I got home, I slept for 36 hours. My family rushed me to the ER, where nurses checked my blood sugar. I was immediately diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. I was in diabetic ketoacidosis, which ends in coma and death without insulin.

When I got out of the ICU, I went to Walgreens to pick up my first 30-day supply of insulin. It cost me $684. I didn’t have that kind of money (most Texans don’t, either) — so I put it on a credit card. I later learned that it costs companies only $10 per vial to produce insulin, but Big Pharma boosts profits by price gouging.

platform.value: Wants to expand the Child Tax Credit, pass paid family leave legislation, and expand access to affordable child care
platform.snippet: Make it easier to start and raise a family: Expand the Child Tax Credit to help families with the cost of raising children, pass paid family leave legislation that would allow Americans to take time off work to bond with a new child or care for a seriously ill family member, and expand access to affordable child care so that no parent has to choose between continuing their career and starting a family.

platform.value: Wants to pass the Older Americans Act Reauthorization Act to expand affordable home- and community-based senior care and build up the elder care workforce
platform.snippet: Make it easier for families to care for their aging loved ones: Increase access to eldercare by passing the Older Americans Act Reauthorization Act to expand affordable home- and community-based care for seniors, and prioritize the development of a high-quality elder care workforce.

platform.value: Wants to pass the Do No Harm Act to protect religious liberty, act against antisemitism/Islamophobia/faith-based hate crimes, and reject forcing religion into neutral public spaces like schools, prisons, courts, and the military
platform.snippet: Defend the separation of church and state and continue to speak out against those who twist the meaning of faith to hurt our neighbors: Pass the Do No Harm Act to protect religious liberty and prevent religious discrimination; take vigorous action against antisemitism, Islamophobia, and other faith-based hate crimes; and reject policies that force religion into neutral public spaces like schools, prisons, courts, and the military.

platform.value: Says he killed legislation that would have established a statewide book ban and removed classic literature like Lonesome Dove and The Catcher in the Rye from public schools, using a procedural point of order
platform.snippet: Killed legislation that would have established a statewide book ban and removed classic literature like Lonesome Dove and The Catcher in the Rye in public schools by using a procedural point of order on the floor of the Texas House.

platform.value: Says he stood up to a proposed THC ban in Texas, arguing it would infringe on individual liberty, hurt veterans, and empower cartels
platform.snippet: Stood up to Texas Republicans’ proposed THC ban, calling out how it would infringe on individual liberty, hurt veterans, and empower the cartels.

platform.value: Says he made progress toward universal paid family leave in Texas by establishing a regulatory framework for employer-issued family leave insurance policies
platform.snippet: Made progress toward universal paid family leave in Texas by establishing a regulatory framework for family leave insurance policies issued by employers.

platform.value: Says he supported young families by providing a liaison officer at each higher-education campus to connect student-parents with health care, employment, transportation, and academic support services
platform.snippet: Supported young families by providing a liaison officer at each campus of higher education to connect student-parents with health care, employment, transportation, and academic success services.

platform.value: Says he authored legislation to legalize regulated marijuana for adults in Texas and use the resulting tax revenue to fund child care and early childhood education
platform.snippet: Authored legislation to legalize regulated marijuana for adults in Texas and use the new tax revenue to fund child care and early childhood education.

platform.value: Says he defended the separation of church and state by leading the fight against legislation to put the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms, replace school counselors with untrained religious chaplains, and add Bible stories to public school curriculum
platform.snippet: Defended the separation of church and state by leading the fight against legislation to force the Ten Commandments into public school classrooms, replace school counselors with untrained religious chaplains, and infuse Bible stories into public school curriculum.

candidates.platform_video_title: I’m running for the U.S. Senate

bio_summary.value: James is an eighth-generation Texan, former middle school teacher, and Presbyterian seminarian. As a state representative, he’s led the fight against the billionaire mega-donors and puppet politicians who have taken over Texas. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate to take his fight against corruption to Washington and win power back for working people.
Hans Truelson (independent) is running for election to the U.S. Senate to represent Texas . He declared candidacy for the general election scheduled on November 3, 2026 .
